behaviour matches the contract on a failed write: executed with an unwritable directory -> recordFailure throws FileNotFoundException (auth maps it to 503 and the error layer logs AuthUnavailableException, OPS errors AC-3), memory keeps the token invalidated so it is still refused, and the next snapshot persists it (restart after snapshot: invalidated=true). Only a disk failure followed by a crash within the 60 s snapshot window loses it; REL-FLOW-001 AC-4 ('on disk before the next snapshot tick') is about a working disk, and no AC requires an immediate retry.

not a defect: issuance requires the account password verified against the re-read (current) hash, and the password alone already regains full access after a ver++ — executed: logout?all=true 204, then a fresh login with only the password 200. A password change also changes the hash, so the old session cannot pass the confirmation. The cross-node staleness is the documented principal-cache window (REL-APIKEY-001: ver++ takes effect within 5 s on other nodes).
